summary.text: Husted is the incumbent Republican, appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. Mike DeWine in January 2025 to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance. A native of northwest Ohio and a University of Dayton graduate, he worked in Dayton-area government and the local chamber of commerce before serving in the Ohio House (2001-2009, Speaker 2005-2009), the Ohio Senate, as secretary of state (2011-2019) and as lieutenant governor (2019-2025). His campaign emphasizes his record in state office.

paragraphs.text: Born in Royal Oak, Michigan, in 1967. According to his Senate office biography, he began life in a foster home before being adopted by Jim and Judy Husted, and was raised in Williams County in northwest Ohio.

Graduated from Montpelier High School and earned a bachelor's degree in education (1989) and a master's degree in communications (1993) from the University of Dayton, where he played football; his Senate bio describes him as an All-American defensive back on the 1989 Division III national championship team.

Worked as a commission assistant to Montgomery County Commissioner Don Lucas (1993-1997) and as a color commentator on University of Dayton football broadcasts. In 1997 he joined the Dayton Area Chamber of Commerce, where he was director and vice president (his Senate bio lists the title Vice President for Economic Development).

Elected to the Ohio House of Representatives in 2000 and served from 2001 to 2009, including as Speaker from 2005 to 2009. According to his Senate office, as Speaker he led passage of a budget that included an income tax cut and created the EdChoice Scholarship.

Served in the Ohio Senate from 2009 to 2011, then as Ohio Secretary of State from 2011 to 2019. He was the named defendant in Husted v. A. Philip Randolph Institute (2018), in which the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Ohio's voter-roll maintenance process.

Served as lieutenant governor under Gov. Mike DeWine from 2019 to 2025, also directing the Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation. His Senate bio credits him with launching the TechCred job-training program and InnovateOhio.

Appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. DeWine on January 17, 2025, to replace Vice President J.D. Vance. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Committees on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions; Small Business and Entrepreneurship; Environment and Public Works; and Appropriations.
According to his Senate office, he and his wife, Tina, raised three children and live in Columbus, where they attend Riverside Church.
